Hi Maya / Raj —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier today. Quick recap + next steps on access controls and support access so we can validate fit for FinTrust's compliance requirements: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Need role-based access controls (RBAC) with least-privilege roles for Product, SRE, and Support.
- Break-glass process for emergency access, fully auditable with time-limited elevation.
- No direct human access to production data by default; support tickets should capture justification.
- Data residency: primary hosting in us-west with EU options if needed later.
- Logging & retention: request for retention windows (audit logs + API request logs) and exportability for audits.

Attached: redwood-rbac-overview.pdf (high-level roles model), support-access-process.docx (support access workflow), break-glass-playbook.pdf (draft).

Next steps I propose:
1) Dev/SE team: Dev, can you confirm whether our RBAC model supports custom roles scoped to datasets and model endpoints?
2) Security: Neha, can you outline what evidence we can provide for break-glass audits and typical retention windows we support?
3) Maya / Raj: please confirm the minimum set of roles you need and whether you have a preferred break-glass approval flow (Slack + ticket, or SSO-based approvals).
4) I'll set up a 30-min follow-up next week to review a proposed policy and map to your procurement timeline.

If you want a live walkthrough of the RBAC UI I can demo it — let me know a couple of times that work.

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Roles: We need at minimum Admin, Platform Engineer, Support Analyst, and Auditor. Support should never have access to raw PII unless explicitly escalated.
2) Break-glass: preferred flow is SSO-based elevation with two-person approval (one on-call engineer + one security approver). Needs an automated ticket creation and an immutable audit trail (who elevated, when, justification).
3) Retention: Audit logs should be retained for 2 years; access logs for 180 days. We need the ability to export logs for internal audits.
4) Support access: we prefer privileged access to be time-bound (max 4 hours) and require justification in the ticket.

Can Dev confirm if Redwood supports time-bound SSO elevation and whether the audit logs include full request payloads or just metadata? Also any constraints on data residency if we later need EU hosting?

Thanks —
Maya Singh
Sr. Security PM | FinTrust
maya.singh@fintrust.com

Hi Maya —

Quick technical notes: 
- RBAC: our runtime supports custom role definitions scoped to resources (model endpoints, project, dataset). You can create roles with a combination of data-plane and control-plane permissions.
- Time-bound elevation: supported via our identity provider integration (SAML/SCIM + IdP-initiated SSO). Elevations can be limited by TTL — we can enforce a max duration (we typically recommend 1-4 hours).
- Audit logs: we capture full request metadata (actor, timestamp, endpoint, query params, model id, tokenization metadata) and for production customers we can include request/response payload logging as an opt-in feature (must be agreed contractually, and we provide redaction controls for PII).
- Break-glass workflow: we support workflow hooks that create a ticket in Jira or ServiceNow and require an approver before elevation. Everything is recorded and exportable as JSON/CSV for audits.
- Data residency: we can provision EU-only tenancy for customer data and logs; cross-region replication is off by default.

I'll attach a short runbook (included by Marissa) and can spin up a demo tenant showing elevation and an audit export.

— Dev

I put together the evidence pack and short demo recording. Items attached: break-glass-export.json (sample export), audit-retention-summary.pdf, redaction-and-pii-guidelines.docx. Key points: 
- We can provide audit exports in JSON/CSV with immutable timestamps and actor details.
